subject: geom/stat smooth formula with a LHS transformation

messages.author: 190470b86061d524
messages.subject: geom/stat smooth formula with a LHS transformation
parts:
I would like to know what the best way to get around the quirk that
formulas with LHS (y) transformations are not being reverse translated
to the correct plotting space. The example code at the bottom should
make it clear what I mean.

My end goal is to use a smoother with the a formula: log(y+1) ~ log(x
+1). I'd like to avoid a procedure similar to http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_smooth.html
because it makes exploratory data analysis difficult when I'm
constantly changing factors or facets. If there's a way to make the
use of models like on the geom_smooth page easily understand changing
factors/facets I'd also be interested in knowing.

I'm still quite new to ggplot2 and R in general so help is very much
appreciated!


# Example:
library(ggplot2)
# Works great
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, cyl)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth
(method="lm", formula= y ~ log(x))

# This smoother is wrong
# geom_smooth draws line the formula without taking the inverse
transormation of the formula (in this case exp(y))
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, cyl)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth
(method="lm", formula= log(y) ~ x)

messages.author: 79cbcdf70bb4b9c6
messages.subject: Re: geom/stat smooth formula with a LHS transformation
parts:
Hi Bob,

As far as I can tell all you need to do is add a coordinate transform
to the y-axis, as in:

(method="lm", formula= y ~ x) + scale_y_log()

You can check that it's the correct model with:

mtcars$pred <- exp(predict(lm(log(cyl) ~ mpg,dat=mtcars)))
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, cyl)) + geom_point() + scale_y_log() +
geom_smooth(method="lm", formula= y ~ x) + geom_line(aes
(y=pred),col="red")

The red curve overlaps the smoother.

Best,

Simon Barthelme
